hook.situation: A friend asks, '주말에 뭐 할 거예요?' You are not reporting what you usually do; you are stating a plan. Korean uses -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for that: 만날 거예요, 갈 거예요, 공부할 거예요. The same frame also works for predictions like 비가 올 거예요.
objectives: Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for future plans and intentions
Choose -ㄹ 거예요 after vowel stems and -을 거예요 after consonant stems
Distinguish a general future plan from a promise made to the listener with -(으)ㄹ게요
hook.whyItMatters: This is the frame learners need for weekend plans, travel plans, homework plans, weather guesses, and 'what are you going to do?' conversations. Without it, you can name activities but not place them clearly in the future.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ 거예요 — saying what you'll do (plans, intentions, predictions)
grammarNotes.func: Use V-(으)ㄹ 거예요 to say what you plan or mean to do, or to guess what will happen. It's the everyday polite way to say "will" or "be going to" — perfect for weekend plans, what you'll eat, or what the weather will do.

formTable.ex: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 보다 → 볼 거예요, 하다 → 할 거예요
먹다 → 먹을 거예요, 읽다 → 읽을 거예요

formTable.add: keep ㄹ, add 거예요 (don't add 을)
formTable.ex: 살다 → 살 거예요, 만들다 → 만들 거예요

examples.en: I'm going to meet a friend tomorrow.
examples.note: 만나다 ends in a vowel, so just add ㄹ 거예요. This is a plan.

examples.en: I'm going to eat at home this evening.
examples.note: 먹다 ends in a consonant, so add 을 거예요.

examples.en: I'm going to watch a movie this weekend.
examples.note: 보다 → 볼 거예요. A simple plan with a friend-talk feel.
Here 오다 is a guess about the weather, not a personal plan — the same form covers both.

keyPoint.label: 거예요 (your plan) vs. 게요 (a promise to me)
keyPoint.body: Both look to the future. -(으)ㄹ 거예요 just states your plan or a guess: 제가 할 거예요 (I plan to do it). -(으)ㄹ게요 is something you promise the listener right now: 제가 할게요 (I'll do it / I promise). Quick tell: weather and other people can take 거예요 (비가 올 거예요), but never 게요 — rain can't promise you anything. You'll practice 게요 more later; for now, default to 거예요 for plans and guesses.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 거예요 is said like [거에요]. The ㄹ before it makes the 거 tense, so 갈 거예요 sounds like [갈 꺼예요] and 먹을 거예요 like [머글 꺼예요].

drill.instruction: Turn each verb into a future-plan sentence with V-(으)ㄹ 거예요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 제가 갈 거 있어요. / 제가 갈게 거예요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Because "I'm going to go" feels like two verbs in English, learners try to bolt on an extra 있어요 or mix in 게. But -(으)ㄹ 거예요 is already a finished sentence ending. Just attach -(으)ㄹ 거예요 straight onto the stem — nothing comes after it.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to meet a friend tomorrow.
exampleSentence.note: 내일 naturally pairs with future plans.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to go to a cafe this weekend.
exampleSentence.note: 이번 주말에 sets the future time frame.
A natural lead-in before using -(으)ㄹ 거예요.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to meet a friend.
I am going to watch a movie this weekend.
I am going to go to a cafe.
I am going to eat gimbap for dinner.
I am going to do homework at home.
I am going to travel during vacation.
exampleSentence.note: 여행을 가다 is the common phrase.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to do homework tonight.

exampleSentence.ko: 내일 약속이 있어서 일찍 나갈 거예요.
exampleSentence.en: I have plans tomorrow, so I am going to leave early.
exampleSentence.note: 약속 often means a social appointment.

exampleSentence.en: I am going to watch a movie with a friend.
I am going to go to a new cafe.
I am going to meet up with a friend.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two friends make weekend plans and adjust them if the weather changes.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
lines.grammarNote: 하다 → 할 거예요. This asks about a future plan.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 토요일에는 친구를 만나서 새 카페에 갈 거예요.
lines.romanization: toyoireneun chingureul mannaseo sae kape-e gal geoyeyo.
lines.en: On Saturday I am going to meet a friend and go to a new cafe.
lines.grammarNote: 가다 → 갈 거예요; 만나서 links the first planned action to the second.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.grammarNote: A natural follow-up that keeps the plan conversation moving.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 비가 오면 집에서 시험공부를 할 거예요.
lines.romanization: biga omyeon jibeseo siheomgongbureul hal geoyeyo.
lines.en: If it rains, I am going to study for the exam at home.
lines.grammarNote: 오면 sets the condition; 할 거예요 gives the planned response.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 저는 영화 볼 거예요. 같이 볼래요?
lines.romanization: jeoneun yeonghwa bol geoyeyo. gachi bollaeyo?
lines.en: I am going to watch a movie. Do you want to watch together?
lines.grammarNote: 볼 거예요 is a plan. 볼래요? asks about the other person's willingness.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Sounds good. When I finish my homework, I'll contact you.
lines.grammarNote: 연락할게요 is a promise to the listener, so -ㄹ게요 is better than -ㄹ 거예요 here.

readingText.title: 이번 주말 계획
readingText.body: 이번 주말에는 조금 바쁠 거예요. 토요일 오전에는 숙제를 할 거예요. 오후에는 친구를 만나서 새 카페에 갈 거예요. 카페에서 커피를 마시고 다음 주 여행 계획을 세울 거예요. 일기예보를 보니까 일요일에는 비가 올 거예요. 그래서 집에서 영화를 보고 한국어 단어를 복습할 거예요. 시간이 있으면 저녁에 산책도 할 거예요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: This weekend will be a little busy. On Saturday morning, I am going to do homework. In the afternoon, I am going to meet a friend and go to a new cafe. At the cafe, we will drink coffee and make plans for next week's trip. According to the weather forecast, it will probably rain on Sunday. So I am going to watch a movie at home and review Korean vocabulary. If I have time, I will also take a walk in the evening.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What will the writer do on Saturday morning?
Find two future plan forms and one prediction form.
comprehensionQuestions.answer: Plans: 숙제를 할 거예요, 카페에 갈 거예요, 복습할 거예요. Prediction: 비가 올 거예요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Why is 갈 거예요 used but 먹을 거예요 would use 을?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 가다 has a vowel-ending stem, so it takes ㄹ: 갈 거예요. 먹다 has a consonant-ending stem, so it takes 을: 먹을 거예요.

culturalNote.title: Plans Are Often Softened
culturalNote.body: Koreans often ask about plans with 뭐 할 거예요? or 주말에 계획 있어요? A direct answer like 친구 만날 거예요 is fine. If the plan is not fixed, soften it with 아마 or 것 같아요: 아마 집에서 쉴 거예요, 카페에 갈 것 같아요. For a promise to the listener, switch to -(으)ㄹ게요: 제가 연락할게요.
culturalNote.tip: Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for your plan; use -(으)ㄹ게요 when you are promising the listener.

inlineExercises.prompt: A friend asks about your weekend plan. Which answer fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: -ㄹ 거예요 presents a future plan or intention.
만나다 has the stem 만나-. Add ㄹ 거예요: 만날 거예요.
먹다 ends in a consonant, so use -을 거예요: 먹을 거예요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is a weather prediction, not a promise?
inlineExercises.explanation: Rain cannot make a promise, so use -ㄹ 거예요 for prediction.

inlineExercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: 제가 연락할 거예요. (You are promising the listener right now.)
inlineExercises.explanation: For a promise or offer made to the listener, -(으)ㄹ게요 is more natural than -(으)ㄹ 거예요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Translate: 'If it rains, I am going to study at home.'
inlineExercises.hint: Use 오면 for 'if it rains' and 하다 → 할 거예요.
inlineExercises.explanation: -면 sets the condition, 'if it rains.' 공부할 거예요 marks the plan or future action that follows from that condition.

inlineExercises.prompt: 주말___ 친구를 만날 거예요. (I will meet a friend on the weekend.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 주말에 marks when the plan happens. 에서 would mark an action place, not the time of the plan.
Consonant-ending stems take -을 거예요 for future plans. 먹다 becomes 먹을 거예요.
내일 sets the future time. 여행을 가다 is the natural chunk for going on a trip, and 갈 거예요 marks the plan.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: '내일 친구를 만나 거예요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: Future plans use the modifier before 거예요. 만나다 becomes 만날 거예요, not 만나 거예요.

bullets: Future arrow: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 points forward to plans, intentions, or predictions.
Vowel stem → -ㄹ 거예요: 가다→갈 거예요, 보다→볼 거예요, 하다→할 거예요.
Consonant stem → -을 거예요: 먹다→먹을 거예요, 읽다→읽을 거예요.
Do not use -ㄹ게요 for weather or third-person predictions; use it for your promise to the listener.

writingTask.prompt: Write 3 sentences about your weekend plans: where you'll go, what you'll eat, and what you'll do.
writingTask.hint: Use V-(으)ㄹ 거예요 for each plan (갈 거예요, 먹을 거예요).
writingTask.model: 이번 주말에 친구를 만날 거예요. 같이 영화를 볼 거예요. 그리고 맛있는 밥을 먹을 거예요.
writingTask.modelEn: This weekend I'm going to meet a friend. We'll watch a movie together. And we'll eat a delicious meal.

canDo: Say a future plan or intention with V-(으)ㄹ 거예요 (갈 거예요)
Choose -ㄹ 거예요 vs -을 거예요 from the 받침 (볼 거예요 · 먹을 거예요)
Make a guess about what will happen (비가 올 거예요)
Talk about weekend and tomorrow plans (주말 · 내일 · 계획)
